---
title: "How to add results"
subtitle: "One folder per run. The site rebuilds itself when you push."
---

## The short version

1. Make a folder in `results/runs/` named `YYYY-MM-DD_short-name`, e.g. `2026-10-21_das3-bb_invdens-r5_10km`.
2. Put your depth-slice images in it, and include the depth in each file name (e.g. `inverted_checkerboard_20km.png`).
3. Add a `run.yml` file (copy one from another run and edit it).
4. Upload the folder to GitHub. The site updates in about two minutes.

You don't have to rename the files your plotting code already writes. The site sorts them like this:

| File name contains | Shown as |
|---|---|
| a number followed by `km` (`..._20km.png`, `z020km.png`) | Recovered slice at that depth, on the depth slider |
| starts with `true` and has a depth (`true_20km.png`) | True pattern at that depth |
| starts with `true` without a depth (`true_checkerboard.png`) | True pattern, shown at every depth |
| anything else (`profile_se-nw.png`, `residuals.png`, `.gif`) | **Other figures**, captioned from the file name |

## Uploading without a terminal

1. Open the repo on GitHub and go into `results/runs/`.
2. Click **Add file → Upload files**.
3. Drag your whole run folder from your computer onto the page.
4. Click **Commit changes**.

## Or from the terminal

```bash
cp -r ~/AlaskaTomography/checkerboard_3D/depth_slices_new results/runs/2026-10-21_my-run
cp results/runs/cb020_das-bb_unweighted/run.yml results/runs/2026-10-21_my-run/
# edit run.yml, then
git add results/runs/2026-10-21_my-run && git commit -m "Add run my-run" && git push
```

## `run.yml` fields

Every field is optional except `title`. Anything you fill in shows up in the run's details table, and the filters on the Results page use `data` and `start_model`.

```yaml
title: Inverse-density, radius 5 km, 10 km checker
date: 2026-10-21
data: DAS + BB            # DAS only | DAS + BB | BB only
cables: [KKFLS, TERRA, KKFLN]
weighting: inverse-density
radius_km: 5
checker_km: 10
anomaly_pct: 5
start_model: alaska-3d    # a folder name in models/items/
picks: synthetic          # a name from Models & data → Pick sets
smoothing_km: 20
iterations: 60
status: done              # done | planned
confirm: false            # true shows a "Details to confirm" tag
source: AlaskaTomography @ <commit>, checkerboard_3D/<folder>
captions:                 # optional captions for "Other figures"
  residuals.png: Initial vs final travel-time residuals
notes: |
  Anything worth remembering for the paper.
```

## Adding SSIM and other metrics

Put a `metrics.csv` in the run folder with one row per depth. Each extra column becomes a line on a small chart under the slider, and its value at the current depth is shown next to it.

```text
depth_km,ssim,corr
10,0.41,0.55
20,0.72,0.81
...
```

## Previewing locally (optional)

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/), then run `quarto preview` in the repo folder.
